subject: Request: one-time latency makegood & staged credit plan for NovaHealth
messages:
From: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@novahealth.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.example, naomi.feldman@redwood.example
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Wed, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spikes affecting NovaHealth triage workflows

Hi Priyom / Naomi,

Thanks for the quick triage earlier this week. We pulled the logs and saw repeated latency spikes across requests to the text-generation endpoint during two windows on 2028-02-24 and 2028-02-27. The attached summary shows 95th percentile latency hitting ~2.8s for a subset of critical endpoints, which caused a backlog in our triage UI and a handful of manual escalations.

We appreciate the on-call response and the temporary routing change you implemented, but NovaHealth’s procurement team is asking for a documented remediation and a concession for the service disruption impacting our incident-handling SLAs. Can you propose the form of concession (credits/discount/free months) and an operational plan to prevent recurrence?

Items we need from Redwood:
- A short post-mortem on root cause + fix timeline
- A remediation / monitoring plan with SLO adjustments if applicable
- Proposed financial concession for the impacted period (invoice credit or discount + how it will be applied)

We’re trying to get this to our CFO/procurement this week.

Thanks,
Dana Lopez
Director of Platform Ops
NovaHealth

Attachment: latency_report_202802.pdf (summary, CSV extracts)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.example>
To: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@novahealth.com>, naomi.feldman@redwood.example
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.example, karthik.iyer@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 1 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spikes affecting NovaHealth triage workflows

Dana — thank you for the note and for the report. I’m sorry for the disruption and appreciate the detail; the latency windows you flagged line up with an autoscaler regression on our serving tier that surfaced under a specific request pattern.

Quick summary of our immediate actions (already executed):
- Temporary routing to warmed instances for the affected routes (reduced errors, which I believe you saw).
- Hotfix to autoscaler threshold; scheduled GCR to validate across traffic patterns.
- Increased 95p latency alert sensitivity and added a supplemental synthetic check for your endpoints.

Proposed remediation + concession (initial ask to execs):
1) Technical: we’ll deliver a detailed post-mortem and a fix validation report by EOD Friday 2028-03-04 and maintain enhanced synthetic monitoring for 60 days.
2) Operational: assign a named CSM (Naomi) and a dedicated on-call from our infra team for two weeks post-fix.
3) Financial concession: a one-time makegood structured as a staged invoice credit totaling 30% of February 2028 bill for NovaHealth, applied as 15% credit on the next invoice and 15% on the following invoice (so it shows in your accounting across the next two billing cycles). If procurement prefers a single invoice write-off we can offer 25% as a single credit instead.

I’m requesting executive approval for the 30% staged credit + the operational remediation package. Marissa / Karthik — can you weigh in on approval and whether we need Legal/Finance sign-off before sending the formal SOW amendment? I’ve attached their latency report for context.

Next steps for us: if you approve the 30% staged credit I’ll prepare the SOW amendment and a DocuSign link for signatures, and Naomi will coordinate go-forward monitoring.

Appreciate your patience — we want NovaHealth to have predictable economics and reliability.

— Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.example
